explanation: The statement is about `ballPoissonIntegral`, which the library defines itself: the Poisson integral over the unit ball of `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)`. It says this integral is zero when the boundary data is zero. The proof just unfolds the definition and simplifies with the general fact that an integral of zero is zero (`integral_zero`), so all of the content sits in the library's own definition. I grepped Mathlib for `ballPoissonIntegral`, `PoissonIntegral` and `poissonKernel`. The only hits were `Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Poisson.lean` and `Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Harmonic/Poisson.lean`; going by their paths, both deal with the complex disc rather than the n-dimensional Euclidean ball, and I did not open them. I found no matching Mathlib declaration.
